description:
Source

Problem / gap
crates/clawft-services/src/api/broadcaster.rs::TopicBroadcaster.topics is a HashMap that never evicts entries. When a ?topic= is subscribed, the broadcast::Sender stays in the map for the gateway's lifetime even when all subscribers drop. broadcast::Sender prunes dead receivers, but the topic slot itself leaks. Long-running gateways with high-cardinality topic names (e.g. sessions:<uuid>, agents:<id>) accumulate idle channel slots indefinitely.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] When the receiver count for a topic falls to zero AND no producer publishes to it for some grace window, the topic Sender is removed from the topics HashMap.
[ ] OR: publish opportunistically drops topics whose receiver_count() == 0 after the failed send.
[ ] Test that simulates a thousand topic subscriptions+disconnects and asserts the map size returns to baseline.
[ ] Document chosen GC strategy in the broadcaster.rs module comment.
Dependencies
None.
Notes
A grace window matters because a producer may publish before any subscriber arrives — but for sessions:* topics the publisher and subscriber lifecycles are coupled via the session itself, so eviction-on-zero-receivers is safe.

/cycles/{id}/cycle-issues/ GET pagination is flaky. Full-list membership counts came back as 1 on two separate reads while the raw first page reported count=100 / total_pages=2+. Membership must be verified via each issue's authoritative issue.cycle_id field, not that listing.

observed during the store-split migration (see the parent item)
Problem / gap
The MCP memory_import tool does not carry the tags column. Verified
empirically with a two-entry probe before the real migration: namespaces and
values are preserved and entries are re-embedded correctly, but tags comes
through empty, created_at is reset to import time, access_count resets to
0, and provenance_type is set to unknown.
So of the 182 migrated entries, the 128 that had tags lost them — 306
distinct tags in total (architecture 17, code 12, security 10,
crate 9, wasm 9, …). Nothing is permanently lost: every tag set, original
timestamp and access count is preserved in the fidelity manifest, keyed by
(namespace, key) with a content sha256.
Why this was accepted rather than fixed inline: neither memory_search nor
memory_list exposes a tag filter in its tool schema today, so tags are
currently unqueryable through the tool surface. Restoring them would have
cost ~128 individual memory_store upsert calls to repopulate a field that no
read path can use. That trade is worth revisiting only when a tag-aware read
path exists.
Acceptance criteria

[ ] If tags are queryable: restore all 128 tag sets from the fidelity manifest

      tag column is populated for exactly those 128
[ ] If tags are NOT queryable: close this item as Cancelled with the reason,
      and keep the manifest as the record
[ ] Either way, record the outcome so the next migration knows the fidelity
      limits up front

Notes
Consider fixing this upstream instead: memory_import honouring a tags

name: ws15: tracker — enforce the two-label rule at item creation (36 items unlabeled, all post-WEFT-556)
description:
Source
2026-07-29 Plane↔git reconciliation sweep, label-coverage analysis
affected set: 36 items, concentrated from WEFT-556 onward
Problem / gap
The project rule requires every work item to carry two labels: a workstream
(wsNN-*) and a finding-type (bug/gap/stub/orphan/governance/
tech-debt/docs/tests/tooling). 36 items violate it: 20 missing both, 14
missing the workstream, 2 missing the type.
The distribution is the actual finding, not the count. Items WEFT-1 through
~WEFT-555 — everything produced by the structured 2026-04-28 release-gate audit
sweep — are fully labeled. Essentially every item from WEFT-556 onward (the
post-audit development wave from ~2026-06-28) is under-labeled.
So labeling discipline did not decay gradually; it stopped when items stopped
being created by the batch triage process. Ad-hoc item creation during
development does not carry the labeling step, because the discipline lived in the
triage protocol rather than in the creation path.
Cost: labels are the only cross-cutting filter. Without a workstream label an
item is invisible to "what's outstanding in voice?", which is how the 0.7.0 audit
findings were made navigable in the first place.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Backfill the 36 items (a proposed mapping was produced during the sweep;
      apply and verify, don't re-derive)
[ ] Make the creation path enforce it, rather than relying on memory —
      the realistic options: make --labels required in
      scripts/plane.sh create-issue, or extend scripts/plane.sh check to fail
      on label gaps and run it in the pre-commit/handoff flow
[ ] scripts/plane.sh check returns clean for label coverage
[ ] The plane-workflow skill states the rule at the point of creation, not
      only inside the triage protocol (§6.1 step 5 currently frames it as a
      triage step, which is why ad-hoc creation skips it)
Dependencies
blocks: nothing functional; degrades tracker navigability
related: the skill's §9 quality bar already asserts "No work item has only a
  workstream label" — the bar exists, nothing enforces it
Notes
ws18-firmware was added during this sweep (the ESP32-S3 firmware stack —
  clawft-edge-pad, clawft-edge-pad-idf, lgfx-bus-rgb-rs, 43 tracked files —
  previously had zero workstream coverage). Include it in the canonical
  references/labels.json set if it isn't already.
Cheapest durable fix is making the wrapper refuse to create an unlabeled item.
  A rule that is only written down has now been demonstrated to lapse the moment
  the surrounding process changes.
